citation: Ruiz-Campillo, X., V. Castan Broto, and L. Westman. 2021. "Motivations and Intended Outcomes in Local Governments' Declarations of Climate Emergency." Politics and Governance 9 (2): 17-28. https://doi.org/10.17645/pag.v9i2.3755.
framework_or_key_measure: Categorises motivations (political positioning, prior environmental action, civil-society pressure) and intended outcomes stated in the declaration text
key_finding_relevant_here: Declarations function mainly as symbolic gestures aimed at raising awareness and shaping future planning, not as commitments with built-in delivery mechanisms; a wording-based read of intent, not a before/after test of what changed

citation: Bush, J., and A. Doyon. 2025. "Climate Emergency Declarations by Local Governments: What Comes Next?" npj Climate Action 4, Article 44. https://doi.org/10.1038/s44168-025-00253-2.
population: 39 Victorian councils that declared a climate emergency
method: Document analysis of declarations and subsequent action plans
framework_or_key_measure: 'Transformative action' framework: mitigation and adaptation together, cross- and intra-council collaboration, links to biodiversity-emergency responses, acknowledgement of First Peoples' knowledges and aspirations, attention to justice and equity
key_finding_relevant_here: Alliances and networks between councils matter for how ambitious the follow-up action plan is; named as one of the two core frameworks in the project brief

citation: Gudde, P., J. Oakes, P. Cochrane, N. Caldwell, and N. Bury. 2021. "The Role of UK Local Government in Delivering on Net Zero Carbon Commitments: You've Declared a Climate Emergency, So What's the Plan?" Energy Policy 154.
population: 308 UK local authorities, city regions and combined authorities that declared a climate emergency
method: Review of published delivery plans against declarations
framework_or_key_measure: No named analytical framework; a completeness check (does a published delivery plan with targets, funding and a timeline exist)
key_finding_relevant_here: Only 2 per cent of authorities had a published delivery plan at the time of declaring; declaration and delivery-planning are shown to be two separate steps, not one event

citation: Hicks, C., K. Davidson, J. H. Lau, et al. 2025. "Implications of Declaration of Climate Emergency on Australian Local Government Policy in the State of Victoria: Policy Analysis Utilising an LLM-Based Retriever-Reader Pipeline." Climatic Change 178, Article 191. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-025-04046-8.
population: Victorian local governments, declared and non-declared, compared
method: LLM-based retriever-reader pipeline (the PALLM tool) applied to council policy documents to detect the presence of 'climate emergency mode' language and content
framework_or_key_measure: A measurable 'climate emergency mode' construct, scored automatically across a large council policy corpus
key_finding_relevant_here: Councils that declared show a greater presence of climate emergency mode in their policy content than non-declared councils; the closest methodological precedent in this list for a before/after, declared-vs-comparison document design

citation: Greenfield, A., S. Moloney, and M. Granberg. 2022. "Climate Emergencies in Australian Local Governments: From Symbolic Act to Disrupting the Status Quo?" Climate 10 (3): 38. https://doi.org/10.3390/cli10030038.
population: 30 Victorian councils that declared a climate emergency, with 3 detailed case studies (Darebin, Moreland, Yarra)
method: Survey of 13 councils plus close reading of 3 councils' action plans against a 10-attribute robust-response checklist
framework_or_key_measure: Symbolic-act-versus-disruption framing; a 10-attribute checklist for what a 'robust' climate response framework contains
key_finding_relevant_here: The 3 case-study councils meet 9 of 10 attributes but do not reach genuine emergency-mode governance (no explicit prioritisation of climate over other council functions); named as the second of the two core frameworks in the project brief

citation: Howarth, C., M. Lane, and S. Fankhauser. 2021. "What Next for Local Government Climate Emergency Declarations? The Gap Between Rhetoric and Action." Climatic Change 167 (3-4), Article 27. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-021-03147-4.
population: 28 London borough councils that declared a climate emergency, January 2019 to January 2020
method: 16 semi-structured interviews with academics, policymakers and civil-society actors
framework_or_key_measure: Four pathways to declaration (actively from above, passively from above, actively from below, passively from across) and three purposes (statement of intent, political gesture, stimulus for local action)
key_finding_relevant_here: Declarations commonly lack an accompanying implementation strategy, funding mechanism or detailed plan; the pathway/purpose framework is a plausible model for why a council signs, separate from what changes afterwards

citation: Krause, R. M. 2011. "Symbolic or Substantive Policy? Measuring the Extent of Local Commitment to Climate Protection." Environment and Planning C: Government and Policy 29 (1): 46-62.
population: Over 1,000 US municipalities that joined the Cities for Climate Protection network
instrument_studied: Voluntary network membership commitment (not an emergency declaration)
method: An index of adopted GHG-reduction policies, built from municipal records
framework_or_key_measure: A symbolic-versus-substantive index, scored from the presence of specific implemented GHG-reduction activities rather than from the commitment's own wording
key_finding_relevant_here: Network membership alone is a weak indicator of actual implementation; policy entrepreneurs inside the council, not the commitment itself, drive substantive follow-through. The closest instrument-level analogue to WALGA's Declaration in this list, since it is a voluntary commitment rather than an emergency declaration

citation: Schulze, K. 2024. "The Soft Channels of Policy Diffusion: Insights from Local Climate Change Adaptation Policy." Policy Studies Journal 52 (4): 881-906. https://doi.org/10.1111/psj.12555.
instrument_studied: Local climate adaptation policy generally, not a declaration or emergency instrument
method: Original survey (2020 to 2021) of municipal administrations, combined with climate-network and public records
framework_or_key_measure: Six-channel diffusion framework: autonomous, collaborative, exemplary, persuasive, organised, funded diffusion
key_finding_relevant_here: Local climate policy change is commonly explained by these diffusion channels rather than by any single triggering event; directly useful for designing Objective 3's comparison group, since it names the confounds a before/after design must control for
